title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness & starvation prevention
author: Asha Menon
body:
Motivation: We observed recurring tail-latency regressions under mixed-priority workloads where low-priority long sequences could monopolize the continuous-batcher queues, leading to starvation of short high-priority requests. This PR introduces scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and per-priority timeouts to improve p95/p99 latency for latency-sensitive routes without compromising throughput for batch-friendly workloads.

Summary of changes: implement a token-aware priority queue for the continuous-batcher scheduler; add configurable per-priority max-queue-time and max-kv-cache-hold; introduce a fairness heuristic that periodically samples queue age and inflight token consumption and force-admits short/high-priority requests; add metrics and alerts for queue-starvation and preemption events; expose new tuning knobs via runtime config and Redwood Console; update unit and e2e perf tests; document rollout plan and recommended defaults.

Key files and modules changed (high level): continuous_batcher/scheduler.go, continuous_batcher/priority_queue.go, continuous_batcher/config.go, continuous_batcher/metrics.go, runtime/config_schema.yaml, docs/operational/continuous-batcher-tuning.md, integration/perf/bench_scheduler_starvation_test.go, examples/quickstart-batching.yaml.

Design notes: the scheduler now maintains separate logical queues per priority class and an LRU-style age index. Each queue tracks cumulative token weight and average head-of-line age. When selecting the next batch, the scheduler computes a fairness score = normalized(1 / (1 + avg_age)) + normalized(1 / (1 + token_weight)) with tunable coefficients. If a high-priority queue has requests exceeding its max-queue-time, the scheduler will preempt tokens from lower-priority queues up to a configured preemption budget. Preemption is conservative and only affects queued requests (not already dispatched KV cache). This preserves throughput while guaranteeing bounded wait-times for latency-sensitive routes.

Configuration: new runtime config section continuous_batcher.scheduler with fields: priority_classes (list), preemption_budget_tokens (int), per_priority_max_queue_ms (map), age_sampling_window_ms (int), fairness_coefficients (list of floats), starvation_alert_threshold_ms (int), enable_preemption (bool). Defaults chosen to be conservative and backward compatible; feature gated behind enable_scheduler_fairness (false by default for rollout).

Testing: added unit tests for priority queue invariants and fairness score computation; e2e perf bench demonstrates p99 latency improvement of 18-32% on mixed workload (70% low-priority long sequences, 30% high-priority short requests) on our canary infra. CI includes a new integration perf job that runs the bench on a small GPU pool.

Compatibility & rollout: behavior is opt-in via enable_scheduler_fairness. We will enable in canary for 72h, validate metrics (queue_starvation_count, preemption_count, p99 latency per route) and then progressively enable for 25%/50% traffic with automatic rollback if regression >5% on p99 for high-priority routes.

Related Linear: ENG-8421 (scheduler fairness work), ENG-8590 (operationalizing preemption knobs).

Checklist:
- [x] Scheduler data structures and token accounting implemented
- [x] Config schema, default values, and feature flag
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Integration perf bench and results attached
- [x] Docs draft for console knobs and recommended tuning
- [x] Alerting rules for starvation and preemption

Notes: This PR intentionally avoids changing KV-cache eviction semantics; a follow-up will evaluate KV cache hold-time strategies to further reduce redundant recomputation.

References: internal benchmarks at /perf/canary/2026-02/scheduler_fairness, previous PRs pr-514321 and pr-527890 for earlier scheduler iterations.

Merge notes: Squash-merged into main after approvals and green CI.

review_comments: Priya Shah (reviewer): Can you clarify how preemption interacts with request cancellation? If a request is preempted while its KV cache is being populated we could waste compute.

Asha Menon (author): Good point. Preemption only affects queued requests that haven't started KV cache population. There's an assert and unit test that ensures we never preempt already-dispatched requests. I'll add clearer comments and a doc note.

Tom Reynolds (reviewer): The fairness score normalization seems sensitive to outliers in token_weight when a single very long sequence is enqueued. Consider using log1p or clipping the token weight before normalization.
Asha Menon (author): Agreed. I switched normalization to log1p(token_weight) and added a unit test covering a 10k-token edge case.
Jing Wei (reviewer): Please add an e2e test that simulates route-level SLAs and verifies the rollout plan and rollback hooks work in CI-staging.
Asha Menon (author): Added an integration perf job in ci/perf-jobs.yaml and a small harness that validates SLA thresholds on canary. See bench_scheduler_starvation_test.go for details.
Priya Shah (approval): LGTM after the doc clarification and one additional perf run on the canary cluster.

release_notes:
- Added queueing fairness and starvation prevention to continuous-batcher scheduler.
- New runtime config knobs for preemption, per-priority timeouts, and fairness coefficients.
- Metrics: queue_starvation_count, preemption_count, queue_age_hist.
- Rollout is opt-in via enable_scheduler_fairness flag.
merge_commit: e7b2a9c - squash: continuous-batcher scheduler fairness and preemption (Asha Menon)
rollback_plan: If canary p99 for high-priority routes regresses >5% after enabling, toggle enable_scheduler_fairness=false on the canary control plane and auto-revert via orchestration. Ops runbook updated in docs/operational/continuous-batcher-tuning.md.
notes_for_ops: Watch metrics: queue_starvation_count > 10 in 5m, preemption_count > 100 in 5m, and p99 per-route. Suggested initial defaults are in the docs. If preemption_count is high, increase preemption_budget_tokens or raise per_priority_max_queue_ms for low-priority classes.
